findings: The former gated fixture generated new context for every UserPromptSubmit, including the second turn that was meant only to consume the earlier idle result. The visible fresh second context plus the production pending-input contract explains why two configured model responses were insufficient in this attempt.

GatedOnce suppresses only later fixture output after the first real hook has written its finished marker. It still starts the Python process and reads the hook input, then returns successful empty output before overwriting either first-run marker.

The first execution retains its actual release wait, original JSON output and actual finished marker. The idle case still requires no idle events/model request, then exactly two requests, distinct turn IDs, the buffered warning on the second ID and context preceding the second prompt.
Immediate uses the same original Python path with a constant False short-circuit guard, so it does not read the finished path or acquire one-shot behavior.
limits: This filesystem existence guard is justified by this fixture's ordered first-finished-before-second-submit protocol; it is not a generally atomic one-shot implementation for arbitrary concurrent hooks.
No third model response, relaxed request count, longer deadline, production hook change, new permission or skip/retry is introduced.
The fixed case and unchanged active-turn immediate case have not yet run. Run them under the original seven-package feature-unified owning context and preserve original diagnostic failure receipts.
